subject: Parametric Bootstraping to test Model fit using Model-averaging

messages.author: 853edef7e17dda88
messages.subject: Parametric Bootstraping to test Model fit using Model-averaging
parts:
Hello,
 I am working with distsamp to fit covariates for detection and abundance.  I have several competing models for one of my species, so I used model averaging for those three models.  However, I would like to test the goodness of fit by using the parametric bootstrapping provided in the package, but I cannot seem to figure out a  way to test the fit for my averaged model.  Is there code that I am missing that would average my models, then give me an object incorporating all of those fitted models that I could then run in this code:

# Function returning three fit-statistics.
fitstats <- function(fm) {
    observed <- getY(fm@data)
    expected <- fitted(fm)
    resids <- residuals(fm)
    sse <- sum(resids^2)
    chisq <- sum((observed - expected)^2 / expected)
    freeTuke <- sum((sqrt(observed) - sqrt(expected))^2)
    out <- c(SSE=sse, Chisq=chisq, freemanTukey=freeTuke)
    return(out)
    }

(pb <- parboot(fm, fitstats, nsim=25, report=1))
plot(pb, main="")

I used the code below to model-average the three top models in my model set, but how do I use parametric bootstrapping for the averaged model?

#Model Average
fl <- fitList(.Practice.Type=m4, .HA_CALC=m3, .Perc.Crop=m12)

SE(fl)

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Parametric Bootstraping to test Model fit using Model-averaging
parts:
hi Alaina,
 I'm pretty sure you CANNOT do this using the capabilities of unmarked although I'm sure if someone has figured it out then they'll say something about it.
 The issue is that parboot() takes a fit object (i.e., a single model) and not a fit list...... 
 
 I recommend testing the goodness-of-fit using the top model.
 
regards
andy

messages.author: 6a288128bce8283d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Parametric Bootstraping to test Model fit using Model-averaging
parts:
Hi Alaina,

We recently did the following in one of our papers (sort of using the averaged model):
"To assess model goodness of fit we used  MCMC iteration to calculate AUC by comparing model results to BUGS estimates of latent occupancy state, using a modification of Zipkin et al. (2012)."

Zipkin, E. F., Grant, E. H. C., & Fagan, W. F. 2012. Evaluating the predictive abilities of community occupancy models using AUC while accounting for imperfect detection. Ecological Applications 22(7):1962–72.

And our paper here:
Schuster, R., Martin, T. G., & Arcese, P. 2014. Bird community conservation and carbon offsets in Western North America. PLoS ONE 11(5):e99292.
As the MCMC approach was only a small part of the study we didn't include the underlying R code, but if you are interested, I could send that to you to provide a starting point.

Cheers,
Richard

Andy,
Thanks for the quick response.  I will keep looking into other ways to do what I need to do, but in the meantime test the goodness-of-fit for the top model. 

Alaina

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: Parametric Bootstraping to test Model fit using Model-averaging
parts: Yeah, I would tend to think that if your global model does not fit well then a model averaged version could not possibly be better.  Model averaging is meant to provide better out-of-sample prediction by avoiding overparameterization, while GOF testing simply suggests whether you have a model that could reasonably have generated the observed data.  So like Andy said, using the global model for GOF testing is probably adequate.
